sections.h2: What happens in the Madison County Clerk's recordings office?
sections.html:
The Recordings Department files the paper trail of land ownership in Madison County: deeds, mortgages, wills, plats and related documents. It operates from the Richmond Branch at 321 N. Madison Ave., Richmond, KY 40475, which keeps counter hours of 8 AM to 4:30 PM. The recordings line is (859) 624-4703, extension 3.

The Berea Branch on Chestnut Street does motor vehicle work, dealer work, marriage licenses, voter registration and delinquent tax payments, and its listing leaves out recordings. The clerk's home page carries a notice that the Richmond branch has relocated, so confirm the street address by phone before you carry an original deed across town.

Electronic submissions are worked each morning until roughly 9:30 to 10:00, and no wait-ons are offered then. Records reach back to 1786. Everything from 1986 onward is scanned for viewing at the counter or online through ECCLIX, a subscription service run by a third party. Searches work on a person's name only, so a street address will not find a deed.

sections.h2: What does a Kentucky deed need before the clerk can take it?
sections.html:
KRS 382.135 spells out the contents and forbids a clerk from lodging a deed that fails them. The closing agent usually drafts the deed, but you can save a rejected filing by confirming spellings and mailing addresses.

  • Full names and mailing addresses for the person giving and the person receiving title.
  • A statement of the price paid.
  • An address where the tax bill for the transfer year may be sent in care of someone.
  • A sworn, notarized certificate from both sides that the price shown is the whole price. On a gift or nominal sale, the certificate says so and puts an estimated fair cash value on the property.

A few deeds skip the price items: utility easements, transfers ordered in a divorce case, corrective deeds between the same parties, rights-of-way for government agencies, and cemetery lots. A swap of properties must state each property's fair cash value in the deed itself.

sections.h2: What will recording cost in Madison County?
sections.html:
The posted schedule bundles a recording fee, an affordable housing trust fund charge and a state clerk fee into one total per document type. The version the clerk publishes carries a 2020 date, so call the recordings line to confirm the amount before mailing a check.

Madison County Clerk totals from the posted 2020 fee schedule
DocumentTotalExtra pages
Deed$50.00$3.00 each past page 5
Mortgage$80.00$3.00 each past page 30
Mortgage release, full or partial$46.00$3.00 each past page 5
Affidavit of descent$50.00$3.00 each past page 5
Power of attorney$50.00$3.00 each past page 5
Will$47.00$3.00 each past page 5
Certified copy$5.0050 cents a page after the third

The same schedule adds $4.00 for each extra reference on a document and $7.00 per notarization. A package that covers several parcels therefore costs more than a single-parcel deed. Notary service at the clerk's counter is offered only for papers being recorded there.

sections.h2: How does the real estate transfer tax work on a Madison County sale?
sections.html:
The grantor owes a half dollar for every $500 of value, and any part of a $500 block counts as a full block. Under KRS 142.050 the clerk calculates the figure from the value declared in the deed and collects it before accepting the document, then certifies the date and amount on the deed itself.

For a sale, value includes the price plus any liens. For a gift or a nominal-price deed, the clerk uses the estimated open-market price. Take the Census Bureau's $232,000 median home value for Madison County: 464 blocks of $500 times $0.50 gives $232.00. A price of $232,100 tips into a 465th block and the tax becomes $232.50. The clerk keeps 5 percent of collections as a fee and remits the rest to the county treasurer every quarter.

  • Foreclosure transfers and deeds given in place of foreclosure owe nothing.
  • Neither do transfers between spouses or ex-spouses in a divorce, partitions, or sales for delinquent taxes.
  • Parent to child and grandparent to grandchild deeds with only nominal payment are exempt too.

sections.h2: How do heirs record an inherited house in Madison County?
sections.html:
For a will, bring the original with the court order attached. The clerk records it, keeps the original, and charges the Will total on the fee schedule. When no will exists, an affidavit of descent under KRS 382.120 goes on record.

A separate duty falls on the personal representative. Before closing the estate, that person files an affidavit with the clerk in each county where the decedent held land, naming the people who receive each parcel and the full or estimated value of each. Heirs planning to sell should ask the probate lawyer whether that affidavit is on file, since a title examiner for the buyer will look for it.

The clerk also runs DocAlert, a free service that emails you when a deed or mortgage is filed under your name. It matches only exact names, so a trust or a business should sign up under every spelling that might be recorded.

sections.h2: Where do unpaid Madison County property taxes end up?
sections.html:
The Sheriff collects first, and the clerk inherits bills that go unpaid. The Sheriff's Office is at 135 W Irvine, Suite B01, Richmond, with a phone number of 859-623-1511 and counter hours of 8:00 to 4:30 on weekdays. Do not mail cash.

Once the bill reaches the clerk, extension 2 on the Richmond line handles questions. The clerk set the sale of the 2025 bills for Thursday, August 27, 2026, at 9 AM in the Fiscal Courtroom of the Courthouse Annex, 135 W. Irvine St. Newspaper advertising must run 30 to 45 days ahead. Bidders register for $250 at least ten days before and post a 25 percent deposit in certified funds. Recording charges on a purchased lien are $30 for the assignment and $46 for a release.

The county bill funds the library, fiscal court, EMS, health department, school board and extension office. Some parcels also pay the Red Lick watershed district, the City of Richmond, the City of Berea or Berea Independent Schools.

sections.h2: What is the Madison County market like for a seller?
sections.html:
Madison County is growing quickly. The Census Bureau puts its 2025 population at 101,696, up 9.7 percent from April 2020, and 62 percent of homes are occupied by their owners. The median home value is $232,000, median rent is $889, and 34.4 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or more.

Richmond, founded in 1798, is the county seat and the home of Eastern Kentucky University. Berea is home to Berea College. The county sits along I-75, with U.S. 25 and U.S. 421 as local routes, and Lexington is about 25 miles northwest of Richmond. Fort Boonesborough, now a state historic site, anchors the county's story, and Madison County was formed in 1785.

Because most recordings happen at closing, request the clerk's current charges and a transfer tax figure for your price before you sign.

faqs.q: Where can a deed be recorded in Madison County?
faqs.a: At the Richmond Branch of the County Clerk, 321 N. Madison Ave. Call (859) 624-4703, extension 3, before you go. Counter hours run from 8 AM to 4:30 PM.

faqs.q: What transfer tax does a Madison County seller pay?
faqs.a: A half dollar per $500 of value, rounded up by block. On a $232,000 sale the bill is $232.00, and the clerk collects it before taking the deed.

faqs.q: Is a notarized price statement required on a Kentucky deed?
faqs.a: Yes. KRS 382.135 calls for a sworn, notarized certificate from both sides that the stated price is the full price paid. A gift deed states that it is a gift and lists the estimated fair cash value.

faqs.q: Are Madison County land records searchable online?
faqs.a: They are, through ECCLIX, a subscription service run by a third party, and every search uses a person's name. Documents from 1986 onward are scanned. Earlier ones are viewed at the Richmond office.

faqs.q: What if property tax goes unpaid in Madison County?
faqs.a: The bill moves from the Sheriff to the County Clerk, gains a lien, and can be sold at the annual tax sale. Call the Richmond line, extension 2, for a payoff before the sale date.
